raidSayLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Kenneth Lynch. Chef. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Wedding ring, Carpenter's square, Dog tags, Coat button, Knife roll. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
Something moves out there — a dog-shaped silence at the treeline.
It followed you. The dog-shaped silence at the treeline is here.
It followed you. The dog-shaped silence at the treeline is here.

💡 COUNTER LEARNED — a dog-shaped silence at the treeline: Wound the lead. Wound the lead and the pack breaks. Hit the FIRST wolf — the one that came in first — and the coordination dies. They fear fire, but breaking the lead is free. (Two survived encounters — the fire has a theory.)
⚔️ Sari stood down the dog-shaped silence at the treeline and kept walking — 3 rounds, bloodied but breathing. It's still out there, somewhere.
⚔️ Morgan stared down the dog-shaped silence at the treeline and it backed off — 0 rounds, not a scratch on them. It's still out there, somewhere.
